name: Central bank stress
summary: Markets price a Fed rate rise in December; yen near 159.3 per dollar after Japanese warnings capped it near 160
state: Markets priced about a 91% chance of a Fed rate rise in December after Governor Waller said on 10 Nov a half-point move could be considered (Trading Economics; MUFG). The yen touched 160.03 per dollar on 12 Nov before Japan's Vice Finance Minister Mimura warned markets not to forget the summer's intervention (MUFG, 16 Nov). The yen was near 159.3 on 18 Nov (Yahoo Finance). No emergency inter-meeting move or new intervention was found.
for_you: Rising rate expectations tend to push up borrowing costs for mortgages and loans. A weak yen raises import costs in Japan and can bring sudden currency moves if officials intervene.
rubric_hit: Watch: stagflationary dilemma with Fed hike priced and Japanese FX intervention warnings near 160 yen; no emergency move (Alert)

sources.title: Trading Economics — Yen Weakens on Fed Rate Hike Expectations

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
